title: Gaming Platform Access Control
instructions: Build a complete access control system for a gaming platform. Write an if/elif/else chain that determines user access based on their account type and account age. Read the rules carefully and test each scenario!
steps: Write an `if` statement to check if account_type equals 'VIP'. If true, print the VIP welcome message.
Add an `elif` to check if account_type is 'Premium' AND account_age is 30 or more. Print the established premium message.
Add another `elif` to check if account_type is 'Premium' AND account_age is less than 30. Calculate days_remaining (30 - account_age) and print a message showing when features unlock.
Add a final `else` block for free/standard members. Print the free member welcome message.

solution:
# Test Case 1: VIP member with 10 days
account_type = 'VIP'
account_age = 10

# Write your if/elif/else structure below:
if account_type == 'VIP':
    print('Welcome VIP! Full access to all games and features.')
elif account_type == 'Premium' and account_age >= 30:
    print('Welcome Premium member! Access to premium games unlocked.')
elif account_type == 'Premium' and account_age < 30:
    days_remaining = 30 - account_age
    print(f'Welcome! Premium features unlock in {days_remaining} days.')
else:
    print('Welcome! You have access to free games. Upgrade for more!')

# After you get this working, test these other cases:
# Test Case 2: Premium with 45 days
# account_type = 'Premium'
# account_age = 45

# Test Case 3: Premium with 15 days
# account_type = 'Premium'
# account_age = 15

# Test Case 4: Free member
# account_type = 'Free'
# account_age = 5
hints: Start with the most specific condition first (VIP), then work your way to more general cases.
For Premium members, you need TWO separate elif statements - one for established accounts (>= 30 days) and one for new accounts (< 30 days).
Use the `and` operator to combine two conditions: `account_type == 'Premium' and account_age >= 30`
To calculate days_remaining: create a variable with `days_remaining = 30 - account_age`, then use it in your f-string.
The `else` block catches everyone who doesn't match the previous conditions - no condition needed after `else:`!
Don't forget colons `:` at the end of each if/elif/else line, and indent the code that should run for each condition.
